authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In the selected development and validation case, the defended mean DDoS-to-Benign rate was lower than the plain attack mean. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance toward the paired preattack reference, but oracle clean recovery is unsupported.

facts.statement: The selected case used a coalition of 10 clients and specified a targeted DDoS-to-Benign label-flip condition.
The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.404618 versus 0.056499 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.097069, an absolute reduction of 0.307549 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert verified malicious intent; the supplied evidence does not establish it.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery; oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and was not substituted.
Refuse to make client-flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decisions; these remain under deterministic pipeline authority.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator was the paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric detector thresholds were not materialized.
The evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
